newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-STONY SILENCE DESCENDS OVER PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STONY SILENCE DESCENDS OVER PSG.

text.p: Paris St Germain's players, their European Super Cup wounds still open, closed ranks on Tuesday and refused to speak to reporters after an intense training session.
Only victory over leaders Monaco in their French league clash on Sunday looks capable of lifting them out of their gloom.

"They have decided not to speak today. They have their reasons, which I respect, but I can't tell you (what they are)," PSG's press officer said after the practice in a biting cold wind at their retreat outside Paris.

The squad had until Sunday only spoken through senior players Rai, Bernard Lama and Paul Le Guen following their 6-1 home defeat by Juventus in the first leg of the European Super Cup at the Parc des Princes last week.
On Sunday, they began their rehabilitation with a 3-0 away win over third division Basancon in the French Cup first round.
Anything less would have compounded their problems and the squad probably needed to make a show of solidarity in the face of adversity and dispel rumours of divisions and cliques among the players.
In the absence of explanations from the players, who may not have a clear, unanimous answer anyway, theories abound as to why PSG crashed so humiliatingly against the world club champions.

PSG had just returned from a sojourn in the tropics and their physical trainer Christian Bourrel said they had banked on the theory that the transition from hot to cold would give them a rush of blood lasting well into the second half.
Instead, Juventus coped far better in the icy conditions as PSG also struggled in new footwear they had not practised with.

The most likely reason is that, apart from catching Juventus on a very good night, they have had thoughts only for Monaco ever since they squandered their lead in the first division in December and allowed their rivals to go four points clear.
The Nicolas Anelka affair has not helped club harmony by allowing a 17-year-old gem to slip through their fingers and commit his future to Arsenal.

With the league championship their priority this season, it remains to be seen whether PSG's training, if it has been aimed since the New Year at Monaco, will peak in the principality's Louis II stadium on Sunday night.
PSG should be at full strength with France defender Alain Roche back in training after injury and assuming key Brazilian playmaker Leonardo recovers quickly from a cold.
